claim: In the ACC's 11 March 2025 cases, FiveM International is alleged to have taken an extra Tk 119 crore 32 lakh 70 thousand from 7,124 workers (accused: owner and former Feni MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, his daughter Tasnia Masud and two others who worked there) and M/s Unique Eastern Private Limited Tk 63 crore 44 lakh 90 thousand from 3,788 (accused: owner Md Noor Ali, his wife Selina Ali, daughter Nabila Ali and former secretary Khondaker Shawkat Hossain).
why_new: Per-agency allegation with worker count and amount.

claim: In the ACC's 11 March 2025 cases, Catharsis International Limited is alleged to have taken an extra Tk 130 crore 43 lakh 22 thousand 500 from 7,787 workers (accused: owner Mohammad Ruhul Amin and his wife Lutfur Nesa Shelly), M/s Ahmad International Tk 143 crore 91 lakh 60 thousand from 8,592 (accused: owner and former Dhaka-20 MP Benzir Ahmad) and BM Travels Limited Tk 135 crore 55 lakh 77 thousand 500 from 8,093 (accused: owner and former Dhaka North councillor Shafiqul Islam and his wife Mousumi Akter).
why_new: Per-agency allegation with worker count and amount.

claim: In the ACC's 11 March 2025 cases, BNS Overseas Limited is alleged to have taken Tk 70 crore 60 lakh 12 thousand 500 from 4,215 workers (accused: owner and Jubo League leader Ishtiaque Ahmed Saikat and his wife Nasrun Nesa), Rubel Bangladesh Limited Tk 47 crore 65 lakh 37 thousand 500 from 2,845 (accused: owner Muhammad Mojibul Haque Rubel and his wife Kamrun Nahar Hiramoni) and The Ifti Overseas an extra Tk 63 crore 59 lakh 97 thousand 500 from 3,797 (accused: owners Md Rubel and Borhan Uddin Panna).
why_new: Per-agency allegation with worker count and amount.

claim: In a memorandum handed to the Chief Adviser's office on 5 May 2025, BAIRA members alleged that in the last round Tk 1 lakh 52 thousand per worker had to be paid to the syndicate, that agencies were made syndicate members for Tk 5 crore each, and that this time Tk 14 crore each was being collected.
why_new: A stated price for an agency's place on the list, last round and in 2025.

claim: The BAIRA members' 5 May 2025 memorandum alleged that the syndicate's ringleaders, Bangladesh-born Malaysian citizen Amin Nor and the fugitive Ruhul Amin, known as Swapan, and their Awami League associates were currently active in forming a syndicate with some influential political leaders, and demanded that Malaysia be asked to scrap the disputed online recruitment software.
why_new: The allegation, a year before the 2026 list, that the same two were rebuilding the ring; Ruhul Amin described as a fugitive.

claim: The memorandum of 5 May 2025 proposed an alternative: BMET would build a database of interested workers, recruiting agencies would take workers from it, the worker would deposit the government-fixed cost through a bank and BMET would supervise the whole process; 453 recruiting agency owners had signed a memorandum with the same demand submitted to the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry on 21 April 2025.
why_new: The agencies' own proposal to cut out brokers and cash, and how many agencies backed opening the market.

claim: Writing in Prothom Alo on 2 June 2025, Dhaka University associate professor and RMMRU researcher Mohammad Rashed Alam Bhuiyan said that in a letter of 23 April 2025, reported by Bloomberg News, Azman Mohd Yusof, secretary general of Malaysia's human resources ministry, called on Bangladesh to review and withdraw 'unsubstantiated allegations' of wrongdoing in labour migration between the two countries in order to improve Malaysia's rating in the annual US trafficking report.
why_new: Malaysia's request that Bangladesh drop the allegations, relevant to how the cases ended.

claim: The same June 2025 column said that Bangladesh's police and Anti-Corruption Commission had begun investigating the recruitment process, that a complaint under the human trafficking law was made against the syndicate, and that in October 2024 Bangladesh police asked the Malaysian government to arrest and return two migration businessmen accused of trafficking migrant workers, money laundering and embezzlement.
why_new: Dates the police request to Malaysia to October 2024 and records the trafficking-law complaint.

claim: On 28 August 2025 a CID sub-inspector, Md Moniruzzaman, filed a money-laundering case at Banani police station against 33 people of the Malaysia labour-market syndicate, among them three former MPs, a former minister's wife and Ruhul Amin, known as Swapan; the case says an inquiry into laundering of money taken by fraud found preliminary evidence of the accused's involvement.
why_new: The CID's money-laundering case: date, station, number of accused.

claim: The accused named in the CID's August 2025 money-laundering case include former Feni-3 MP Masud Uddin Chowdhury, his wife Jesmin Masud and daughter Tasnia Masud, Ahmed International's owner Benzir Ahmed, Snigdha Overseas Limited's proprietor Nizam Uddin Hazari, Kashmeri Kamal of Orbitals Enterprise, and Ruhul Amin, former BAIRA secretary general and owner of Catharsis International; the case was filed under the Money Laundering Prevention Act.
why_new: Who is named and under which Act.

claim: On 4 November 2025 the Anti-Corruption Commission approved six cases against 11 owners and officials of six recruiting agencies, alleging that on average five times the government-fixed Tk 78,990 was collected from 31,331 Malaysia-bound workers and Tk 525 crore 22 lakh 97 thousand 500 embezzled and laundered, its director general Md Akhtar Hossain said on 6 November.
why_new: The third batch of ACC cases, with date, workers and amount.

claim: The ACC cases approved in November 2025 allege extra collections by M/s Amin Tours and Travels (owner Ruhul Amin) of Tk 124 crore 45 lakh 25 thousand from 7,430 people, by M/s Merit Trade International Limited (chairman Hasan Ahmed Chowdhury Kiron) of Tk 58 crore 44 lakh 7 thousand 500 from 3,489, and by Sadia International (Shamim Ahmed Chowdhury alias Noman) of Tk 55 crore 62 lakh 67 thousand 500 from 3,321.
why_new: Per-agency allegation with worker count and amount.

claim: The ACC cases approved in November 2025 also allege collections by Imperial Resource Limited (chairman Md Iqbal Hossain, managing director Badruddoza Chowdhury) of Tk 135 crore 69 lakh 17 thousand 500 from 8,101 people, by RRC Human Resource Service Limited (chairman Mohammad Moniruzzaman, managing director Md Alamgir Kabir) of an extra Tk 87 crore 13 lakh 35 thousand from 5,202, and by Thanex International Limited (former manager Abdullah Shahed, director Md Joynal Abedin Nomani, current manager Shamser Ahmed) of an extra Tk 63 crore 88 lakh 90 thousand from 3,788.
why_new: Per-agency allegation with worker count and amount.

claim: Before the November 2025 cases the ACC had filed cases on 11 March 2025 against 32 people over Tk 1,128 crore and on 14 September 2025 against the top officials of 13 recruiting agencies over Tk 1,159 crore, all over sending workers to Malaysia.
why_new: Gives the three ACC batches together: 12, 13 and 6 agencies.

claim: Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch (DB) arrested Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a former Feni-3 MP who had obtained a recruiting licence, at his home in Baridhara DOHS, Dhaka, at midnight on a Monday (reported by Prothom Alo on 24 March 2026), and a court granted five days' remand in a human trafficking case of Paltan police station.
why_new: The first reported arrest of a syndicate agency owner; the guide records cases and licence cancellations but no arrest.

claim: The Paltan police station case in which Masud Uddin Chowdhury was remanded was filed on 3 September 2025 by Altab Khan, owner of a firm named Afia Overseas, alleging embezzlement through a syndicate and human trafficking, and names 103 accused in all.
why_new: A trafficking case against the syndicate brought by another agency owner, with 103 accused.

claim: A DB additional commissioner said in March 2026 that Masud Uddin Chowdhury faces 11 cases in Feni and Dhaka, including cases at Dhaka's Paltan, Banani, Kotwali, Mirpur and Hatirjheel police stations on charges including murder, attempted murder and human trafficking, and that the ACC and the CID are investigating several allegations against him; at the remand hearing the public prosecutor said the accused had made off with Tk 24,000 crore in the name of sending people abroad.
why_new: Number and kind of cases pending against one syndicate agency owner.

claim: Prothom Alo reported that Masud Uddin Chowdhury went into business after retiring in 2014, later obtained a manpower-export (recruiting) licence, and was then accused of making huge sums through the syndicate for sending workers to Malaysia.
why_new: Background of the owner of the top Malaysia sender.

claim: A law-enforcement source told Prothom Alo in March 2026 that the ACC has a case against Masud Uddin Chowdhury alleging embezzlement of Tk 119 crore and has applied to the court to show him arrested in it, and that the court fixed 9 April 2026 for an order; a DB joint commissioner said he was on remand in a specific case and that information obtained from him was being verified.
why_new: Where the ACC's Five M case stood a year after filing: the accused only now being shown arrested.

claim: Sources involved in the questioning told Prothom Alo that Masud Uddin Chowdhury is being asked how he used the state machinery in starting a manpower-export business after retirement and in allegedly building a syndicate in the name of sending workers to Malaysia and embezzling large sums.
why_new: What investigators are asking about.

claim: On 19 July 2026 the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry issued a notification withdrawing the licences of 49 recruiting agencies, including agencies of former Awami League MPs, that Prothom Alo linked to the Malaysia syndicate; the notification says charge sheets against them under sections 406, 420, 385, 386, 427 and 34 of the Penal Code 1860 were filed in court and accepted, and that the licences were withdrawn under the migration Act for that reason.
why_new: The Malaysia doc says 49 licences were cancelled in July 2026; this adds the exact date, the legal ground (an accepted charge sheet) and the Penal Code sections. The date 19 July is confirmed by article 2ec8c523.

claim: Among the 49 agencies whose licences were withdrawn on 19 July 2026 are Orbitals Enterprise and Orbital International, owned by the wife and daughter of former Awami League finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal; Ahmed International of Benzir Ahmed, MP for Dhaka-20; Snigdha Overseas Limited of former Feni-2 MP Nizam Uddin Hazari; and Five M International of former Feni-3 MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury.
why_new: The Malaysia doc names only Catharsis among the 49; these are the politically owned agencies, named with their owners.

claim: The 49 agencies whose licences were withdrawn on 19 July 2026 also include Unique Eastern Private Limited, of Noor Ali, whom Prothom Alo calls a much-discussed manpower businessman, and Catharsis International, of Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, whom it calls one of the members of the Malaysia syndicate.
why_new: Adds Unique Eastern (Noor Ali) to the named withdrawals; Catharsis is already in the doc.

claim: The other agencies whose licences the Ministry withdrew on 19 July 2026, as named by Prothom Alo, include: M/s Shaheen Travels, Irving Enterprise, Hridoy Trade International, Rabbi International, Jahrat International, 4 Site International, Binimoy International, Akash Bhraman Limited, QK Quick Express Limited, United Export Limited, GMG Trading Private Limited, Sadia International, The Super Eastern Limited, Elegants Overseas Limited, Midway Overseas Limited, Madina Overseas, Al Khamis International, New Age International, Damashi Corporation Limited, Galaxy Corporation, Sultan Overseas, Provati International, Manispower Corporation, Amin Tours and Travels, ISMT Human Resource Development, Darbar Global Overseas, Natasha Overseas, Aparajita Overseas, Stanford Employment Private Limited, Jannat Overseas, BM Travels, BNS Overseas Limited, Rubel Bangladesh Limited.

why_new: The doc points to agency records for the syndicate agencies but names none of the 49; this is the printed list (42 names besides the seven named with their owners). English spellings are transliterated from the Bangla and should be matched to RL numbers on OEP; the article prints no licence numbers.

claim: The other agencies whose licences the Ministry withdrew on 19 July 2026, as named by Prothom Alo, include: Trans Asia Integrate Services Limited, Al Farah Human Resources and Consultancy, Brothers International, Thanex International Limited, JG Alfalah Management, Imperial Resources Limited, PR Overseas Limited, MEF Global Bangladesh Limited, Ananya Apurba Recruiting Agency.
placement: other: Action in Bangladesh (list of the 49; belongs with the agency records)
why_new: The doc points to agency records for the syndicate agencies but names none of the 49; this is the printed list (42 names besides the seven named with their owners). English spellings are transliterated from the Bangla and should be matched to RL numbers on OEP; the article prints no licence numbers.

claim: When Malaysia reopened in July 2022 after nearly four years, the selection of agencies was left to the Malaysian government, to which the Ministry sent a list of 1,520 recruiting agencies; the syndicate began with 25 agencies and grew in three steps to 100, and it is alleged that a large sum was taken from each agency to get its name in.
placement: other: how the 2022-24 syndicate was formed
why_new: The doc describes the 2026 list of 25 but not the 2022 numbers: 1,520 proposed, 25 chosen, then 100, with an alleged entry payment by each agency.

claim: The NCP's spokesperson, Asif Mahmud, said in a statement on 22 August 2026 that the Bangladesh government had earlier sent Malaysia a list of 423 recruiting agencies that met Malaysia's conditions, and that the process, criteria and basis on which only 25 were chosen from it were still not clear.
why_new: The doc says a Malaysian committee chose the 25 but not that they came from a Bangladesh-approved list of 423, or that the selection criteria were never published.

claim: Several members of BAIRA, the recruiting agency owners' association, told Prothom Alo in September 2026 that the earlier syndicate agencies and the firms of ministers or MPs are not directly on the new list, but that the old ringleaders of the syndicate are behind the unfamiliar agencies, and that workers may have to spend Tk 6 to 7 lakh to go this time.
why_new: Explains, as BAIRA members allege it, why the 2026 list is made of unknown agencies: they front for the earlier organisers.

claim: Prothom Alo reported in September 2026 that Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, a former BAIRA secretary general alleged to act in Bangladesh as the representative of Amin Nur, has been in hiding abroad since the fall of the Awami League in the 2024 uprising, that his agency's licence has been withdrawn, a case against him is under way and the ACC is also investigating.
why_new: The doc says police sought his extradition; this adds that he is abroad in hiding and the state of the proceedings as of September 2026.

claim: Prothom Alo reported in September 2026 that Bestinet owns Migrams, the software of Malaysia's FWCMS recruitment system, and is owned by Aminul Islam bin Abdul Nur, a Malaysian citizen of Bangladeshi origin known as Amin Nur.
why_new: Adds the software's name (Migrams) and the name "Amin Nur" by which he is known in the Bangla press; the doc calls him "Amin".

claim: The state minister for expatriates' welfare, Md Nurul Haque, told Prothom Alo in September 2026 that the Ministry would set a cost ceiling for sending workers to Malaysia, and that if any agency accused of trafficking or corruption is on the list Malaysia would be told and its licence withdrawn.
why_new: A dated commitment by the state minister on two open points in the doc: a cost cap, and removal of accused agencies from the list.

claim: In a notice of 28 August 2026 the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry said the agencies were vetted by a high-level joint committee of Malaysia's human resources, foreign and home ministries, its anti-corruption commission and law enforcement agencies, with not the slightest involvement of the Bangladesh government.
why_new: The doc says "a Malaysian committee"; this gives its composition and the date of the Ministry's notice. Note: the same notice, as printed, dates the MoU to 18 December 2022.

claim: Prothom Alo reported that Malaysia set 10 conditions for the agency list, that 163 agencies first qualified, and that after Malaysia relaxed three conditions and then one more at Bangladesh's request, the Ministry under the interim government sent Malaysia a final list of 423.
why_new: How the long list was made (10 conditions, 163 qualifying, 423 after four conditions were relaxed); not in the doc. The article does not say what the conditions were.

claim: Prothom Alo reported in September 2026 that Malaysia approved 25 agencies each for Nepal and Bangladesh and 10 each for India, Pakistan and Myanmar, that the agency owners' associations of four countries protested in a joint statement, that everyone on the lists sent by countries such as Sri Lanka and the Philippines was approved, and that Nepal has begun an investigation into its list of 25.
why_new: Comparison with other source countries in 2026, absent from the doc: the limited list is no longer unique to Bangladesh, and Nepal is investigating its own.

claim: Shariful Hasan, associate director and head of BRAC's migration programme, told Prothom Alo in September 2026 that the choice of 25 agencies proved the syndicate is stronger than the two governments, and that workers are again being recruited through Amin Nur's system.
why_new: A named expert's assessment that the 2026 arrangement runs on the same system as 2022-24.

claim: On 4 October 2026 the Appellate Division's chamber judge, Justice Md Rezaul Haque, stayed a High Court order that had suspended the Ministry's 19 July 2026 notification, so the withdrawal of the 49 recruiting agencies' licences remains in force.
why_new: The doc records the July withdrawal but not that agencies challenged it and that it was upheld (so far) at the Appellate Division in October 2026.

claim: The Attorney General, Md Ruhul Quddus Kajal, said that after one agency challenged the withdrawal by writ the High Court issued a rule and stayed the notification on 15 September 2026, the chamber court stayed that order on 30 September, and 11 more agencies then obtained a stay from a vacation bench in a second writ, which the chamber court also stayed; Prothom Alo names New Age International among the agencies that filed writs.
why_new: The sequence of court orders: for two weeks in September 2026 the withdrawal was suspended, which matters to anyone checking whether one of the 49 could legally recruit on a given date.
